title: Jetts vs Encore Pilates NZ – Which Gym Is Best for You?
meta_desc: Compare Jetts and Encore Pilates NZ on price, contract, facilities, 24/7 access and value. Find out which budget or boutique gym fits your goals and schedule.
intro: Choosing between a low‑cost, all‑day gym and a boutique Pilates studio can feel like comparing apples and oranges. Both Jetts and Encore Pilates offer no‑joining‑fee, no‑lock‑in memberships, but they serve very different workout goals. Below is a practical side‑by‑side look to help you decide.

Selected cities, 3 studios in Bay of Plenty

sections.heading: Price, contract and cancellation
sections.body:
Jetts positions itself as a budget gym with weekly rates from $14.95 to $19.95, depending on the chosen tier and any current promotions (e.g., 15% off + 4 weeks free). There is absolutely no joining fee and no lock‑in contract, meaning you can walk away after a single week without penalties. This makes Jetts an attractive option for students, travellers, or anyone testing a gym for the first time.

Encore Pilates charges $22.00–$50.00 per week, reflecting the boutique nature of its reformer‑based classes and smaller studio environment. Like Jetts, there is no joining fee and no long‑term contract, so you can cancel at any time. The higher price point is justified by specialised equipment, smaller class sizes and a focus on core‑strength work.

Both brands are eligible for the Exercise NZ subsidy, which can knock 40–70 % off the weekly fee for eligible members (new members or those inactive for 12+ months). This can bring Jetts down to roughly $4.50–$8.00 per week and Encore Pilates to $9.00–$20.00 per week, depending on the subsidy level.
list: Encore Pilates: $22.00–$50.00/week, no contract, cancel anytime.
Exercise NZ subsidy can reduce both fees by 40‑70 % for eligible members.

sections.heading: Facilities, classes and access
sections.body:
If you need a gym that’s open around the clock, Jetts delivers with 24/7 access, free parking and a full suite of free‑weight and cardio machines. However, it does not offer group fitness classes, so you’ll be on your own for motivation unless you hire a personal trainer.

Encore Pilates focuses on reformer Pilates, group fitness and post‑natal programmes. Classes fill quickly, so booking in advance is essential. The studios lack 24/7 access and dedicated parking, but the specialised equipment and small‑class environment provide a higher level of instructor guidance and core‑strength development.
list: Jetts – ideal for self‑directed cardio, strength training, and night‑owls.
Encore Pilates – best for structured Pilates, core work, and community‑driven classes.
